html:
The War of Canudos was a conflict between the Brazilian republic and a religious community at Canudos, in the backlands of Bahia, from 1896 to 1897. The army destroyed the town, and many thousands died.

The wandering preacher Antônio Conselheiro founded Canudos in 1893. Poor farmers, former slaves and Indigenous people flocked to it, and it grew to tens of thousands. It refused to pay republican taxes, and the new republic, founded after the fall of Pedro II, saw it as a monarchist threat. Three army expeditions were beaten. A fourth, with thousands of soldiers and artillery, took the town house by house.

Most of the defenders were killed, many after surrendering. The journalist Euclides da Cunha, who covered the war, wrote Os Sertões (1902), a classic of Brazil that showed the gap between the coast and the backlands. Mario Vargas Llosa retold the story in his novel The War of the End of the World (1981).
